business: Money Spending Board (personal budgeting web app, Thai and English)
why_not: I already keep a spreadsheet for my freelance income and card bills, and it works. Setting up an iPhone Shortcut and handing my bank slips to an app to save me a few minutes a week does not feel like enough of a gain yet, even at 69 baht.

The card statement import would save me some retyping once a month, but I only do that job once a month and it takes me about ten minutes anyway, so 69 baht a month for it is hard to justify. The slip part needs me to remember to scan every day, and I already know I won't keep that up.

The free part already does what I need, and the paid part only matters if it reads my K PLUS and card statements properly. I'd try the free trial, but I wouldn't pay anything until I've seen it work on my own slips and statement, and I'm not convinced a new app should be reading my bank data.

I already have free budget apps that do the basic tracking, and I don't want to hand a new app my bank slips or my card statement, even if it's only the text. The features that matter most to me are the ones that need the most trust, and I don't know this company.
My bank app already shows my history, so I don't see what this adds beyond it. I'd maybe try the free trial to see, but I'm not paying for slip reading I could just look up in my banking app.

My bank app already shows my transfer history, so I don't feel I'm missing anything. I'd have to set up a Shortcut on my iPhone and log into another app just to see slips I can already find in one place.

69 baht is nothing, and I like the 50/30/20 split. But the iPhone Shortcut looks like a fiddly one-time setup, and I'd only pay once it actually reads my K PLUS slips without me fixing things every time.

I like the idea of having all my bank slips in one place, but the Shortcut setup sounds like a chore, and I'd have to trust a budgeting app with my bank slip text. I'd rather try the free manual tracking first and see if I keep using it.

Keeping my bank slips in one place is exactly what I want, but the page only names K PLUS, Bangkok Bank and TTB, and I use a different bank. I would not pay for something that might not read my slips.
flip: Seeing my own K PLUS slip and my card statement read correctly during the free trial, with a clear explanation of what gets stored and how it is encrypted.
If I could try the card statement import on my own statement for free, see my categories filled in correctly, and confirm the data stays on my side or is clearly explained.
If the statement import alone cost much less, or if scanning a slip took a couple of seconds at the moment I pay, so I didn't have to remember it later.
A monthly breakdown by category that my bank app doesn't give me, built automatically from my slips and card statement, that I actually kept using for a full month during the trial.
If it could pull my slips and card statements into my own spreadsheet automatically with no setup, and I could export everything, I would reconsider.

A clear, independently checked privacy policy with a way to delete all my data and no need for my statements, plus a free version that works well enough that I could see the value before paying anything.
A setup that takes a couple of minutes with no fiddling, and a way to export to my own spreadsheet so I don't feel locked in.
If it pulled my K PLUS and credit-card spending into one list that my bank app doesn't show, and the setup took only a few minutes.
If the trial showed that the statement import and slip capture cut my monthly entry time to almost nothing, with accurate categories and no fiddling.
If the free trial correctly categorised my own card statement with little fixing, so that it saved me more time each month than the spreadsheet costs me.
Seeing it correctly read three or four of my own real K PLUS slips and a real card statement during the free trial, with my bank clearly supported.
A plain statement that only the recognised text is kept, that I can delete all of it, and a clear list showing K PLUS, BBL and TTB slips work before I pay anything.
A way to import my K PLUS or BBL transactions automatically, with no daily scanning from me.
If it saved me real time every week, with setup no harder than the video, and it did something my spreadsheet cannot do on its own.
Seeing it work on my own K PLUS slips during the free 14-day trial, with the setup finished in a few minutes and no errors.
A clear list showing my bank and my card's statement format are supported, or a trial that reads my own slip correctly on the first try.
A list of the banks and card issuers it reads, and a trial where my own slip or statement comes through correctly before I'm charged.
If it pulled my credit-card statement in and sorted the categories better than I do now, with almost no setup, and I could export my data out if I left.
If it reminded me or picked up my slips automatically without me having to do anything each day.
If the setup took about five minutes on my phone, and I could turn it off and delete my data without fuss.
